updates.bio: Zuni Pueblo artist and communications and outreach specialist who in late 2016 became the first artist-in-residence of the Community Environmental Health Program at UNM's College of Pharmacy. Working with Indigenous knowledge keepers and investigators on projects such as METALS, Quetawki creates paintings and digital art that make biochemical and health research culturally relevant for partner Native communities.
updates.research_interests: culturally inclusive science communication; Indigenous-centred art for environmental health research; two-way communication between researchers and tribal communities

updates.bio: Chosen in 2020 by NOAA's Office of National Marine Sanctuaries as the first superintendent of the new Mallows Bay-Potomac River National Marine Sanctuary. At NOAA since 1983 and with the sanctuaries office since 2002, he earlier headed its Technical Programs and Support Division and worked with Chesapeake community coalitions. He holds a University of Maryland master's in marine-estuarine-environmental sciences.

updates.bio: Scientist at UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography from 1956 until he died in 2005, made professor of oceanography in 1968. In 1958 he began surveying carbon dioxide in background air, including measurements at Mauna Loa Observatory that continued under his guidance; his interests centred on the carbon cycle, atmospheric chemistry and air-sea CO2 exchange.
updates.research_interests: carbon and oxygen geochemistry; atmospheric chemistry; natural carbon cycle; atmospheric carbon dioxide levels and their air-sea exchange
updates.current_affiliation: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, University of California San Diego

updates.bio: Distinguished Professor at CU Boulder's Institute of Arctic and Alpine Research (INSTAAR). A limnologist, McKnight examines how hydrologic, chemical and biological processes jointly control freshwater ecosystems, including trace metals and natural organic matter in Rocky Mountain and McMurdo Dry Valleys streams and lakes, and is a co-PI of the McMurdo Dry Valleys and Niwot Ridge LTERs.
updates.research_interests: limnology; biogeochemistry of lakes and streams; how freshwater organisms interact with trace metals and natural organic matter; watershed and mine-drainage problems in the Rockies
updates.current_title: Distinguished Professor; Co-editor, Arctic, Antarctic and Alpine Research
updates.current_affiliation: Institute of Arctic and Alpine Research (INSTAAR) and Environmental Studies, University of Colorado Boulder
updates.evidence: I'm a co-principal investigator in the McMurdo Dry Valley LTER and in the Niwot Ridge LTER.

updates.bio: Regents Professor of Ecology Emeritus in Montana State University's Department of Land Resources and Environmental Sciences, having joined MSU's faculty in 1984. Trained in microbial ecology (PhD, UC Davis), Priscu has led Antarctic research teams since 1984, was chief scientist of the SALSA and WISSARD subglacial lake drilling projects, and co-directs MSU's Subzero Research Facility.
updates.research_interests: biogeochemistry and microbiology of icy environments; long-term Antarctic lake ecology; Arctic lake methane dynamics; exploration and geomicrobiology of Antarctic subglacial lakes; microbiology, geochemistry and paleoclimate of ice cores

updates.bio: Executive Director of the MassBays National Estuary Partnership since 2026, after serving as its program scientist from 2010. Vella sets program direction, manages staff, works with five regional service providers and agency partners, and leads work under the program's management plan. Degrees: biology, chemistry and marine biology (University of Malta); environmental science and policy (UMass Boston).

updates.bio: Habitat Program Manager at the MassBays National Estuary Partnership, coordinating environmental monitoring and coastal habitat mapping. Carr helps non-governmental groups plan projects, analyse and visualize data and get it to decision-makers, favouring interdisciplinary work that restores, inventories and protects coastal habitats. Education: coastal studies B.S. (UConn) and geo-information science and remote sensing M.S. (Salem State).
updates.research_interests: environmental monitoring; coastal habitat mapping; data analysis and visualization for management; coastal habitat restoration and inventory
updates.current_affiliation: MassBays National Estuary Partnership (University of Massachusetts Boston)
